body.p: After (sequence representations), (reverse of a range in O(1)) and (item demands). Running SchXslt 1.10.1 on sxml to compile the EN 16931 Schematron rules (2026-10-28) found that recursing over the rest of a sequence is quadratic: make_span in src/function_library_sequence.c copies every item after the start into a new vector unless the input is an integer range, so fn:tail, fn:subsequence and $s[position() > 1] cost the length of the rest. Measured (release, x86_64 Xeon 2.1 GHz): one recursive walk over 780 elements takes 106 ms with $items[position() > 1], 28 ms with tail($items), 32 ms with subsequence($items, 2). SchXslt's schxslt:replace-params walks 780 parameters this way for each of 1,042 attributes: about 110 s of its expand stage (8 min 56 s in all, 1 min 39 s once its own per-level re-sort is removed; about 9 s of that is fn:replace). The compiled rules themselves pass all 1,133 checks of the EN 16931 UBL unit tests.

item.p: Mechanism: general mechanisms of the one evaluator, no Schematron-specific machinery: a slice of a stored sequence (a vector, or another slice) shares the stored items instead of copying them, so fn:tail, fn:subsequence, fn:slice, fn:head and fn:trunk of one are O(1); $s[position() > N], $s[position() >= N] and $s[position() = N to M] with N and M fixed for the filter take the same path (an IR pass, or the evaluator's FILTER fast path). Prefer a representation internal to src/xdm_sequence.c (a slice cell referring to its base cell); a new public sxml_sequence_representation is an additive change to a frozen header () and needs its own decision record first. Reference counts keep the base alive while a slice exists; a small slice of a large base may be copied when the base would otherwise outlive it (state the rule and its threshold in the D-record). "Slice" already names QT4 test lists in docs/GLOSSARY.md (); add the new term there first under a name of its own (for example ).

Owns: src/xdm_sequence.c, src/function_library_sequence.c, the FILTER parts of src/evaluator.c and src/ir_loop_passes.c, tests/bench/ (a new recursion-tail.xq with the three forms), tests/xdm_sequence_test.c.

Done when: the three forms walk 780 items in time linear in the length (before and after in the D-record and the commit messages); SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931, unpatched, measured before and after; no QT4 XP40, XQ40 or XT40 outcome changes, case by case; , the memory limits and honest step counts kept (a slice step counts one). Done 2026-10-28 (): sequence slices (a cell over a vector, reported as a vector; spans of at most 16 items or under an eighth of the base copied), positional filters in the evaluator's FILTER, and a matched-base memo for typed parameters; 100 walks over 780 elements 10.23, 2.55, 3.03 s to 0.11 s each, linear; SchXslt's expand stage 552 to 458 s; QT4 XP40, XQ40 and XT40 whole: 0 outcomes differ.
